summary: Observations of three very bright points moving West-East in the clear sky: observations of elements of the Dragon spacecraft supplying the International Space Station (ISS).
description: On December 15, 2017, at 6:33 PM, two witnesses were intrigued by the movement of three very bright points in the sky. The three points were perfectly aligned and moving from west to east. The observation lasted 30 seconds. The two witnesses observed three objects in the same orbit: the Dragon resupply spacecraft for the International Space Station (ISS), accompanied by the two protective elements for its solar arrays. The launch of this mission (CRS-13) took place from Florida at 4:36 PM (local time in France), and the observation occurred approximately two hours later, which explains why the three objects were still very close together. These three objects are cataloged by the US Space Command under the numbers 43060 to 43062 (international designation 2017-080 A to C). Images including these same three objects plus the upper stage of the launch vehicle had already been published online during the launch of the CRS-11 mission (see the video Dragon resupply Mission CRS-11). In this case, since the upper stage had already completed its re-entry ignition, only three objects remained visible. GEIPAN classifies the case as A: elements of the Dragon spacecraft for resupplying the International Space Station (ISS).

summary: Observation from a moving vehicle and through a smartphone of a small circular fluorescent green teche in the landscape: photographic artifact.
description: On December 7, 2017, at 3:12 PM, a witness in a taxi was observing and photographing the clouds with a smartphone. A circular, fluorescent green spot that appeared stationary or moving at the same speed as the taxi particularly intrigued him. The witness took several photographs and then, a little later, recorded a video. Only one witness statement was collected. The witness was searching for "elementals" or "beings of life" and believed he had found one following him through the landscape and bushes along his taxi route. In fact, it is clear that the witness was being misled by a reflection of the sun created by his smartphone camera. In the photo taken at 3:16:29 PM, the sun is off-center, and the slightly green spot or UFO with a halo is the classic reflection created by imperfect optics, which reproduces (in a less bright form) any extremely bright point, in this case the sun, symmetrically around the center of the image. In the photo at 15:16:42, the sun is not in the center either; the reflection is still present but falls into an already very bright area of the image (the luminous cloud) and therefore does not appear. In the photo at 15:16:18, the reflection falls into the bush in the foreground. The same phenomenon is observed in the video footage. GEIPAN no longer accepts reports of strange occurrences based solely on what is seen on a device screen and not with the naked eye. One might have thought that the witness had verified it visually since he wrote, "I then checked by moving my screen to look at this curious green spot in the bushes and that the spot was indeed there." Analysis of the entire testimony leads us to reject this verification: - firstly, the witness makes no distinction between a UFO seen with the naked eye and one that actually exists on the screen and is created by the optics; - secondly, the witness displays such eagerness to find anomalies in the landscape that we can question their critical thinking. Perhaps unwittingly, they believe they saw the glow with the naked eye in the bush, fleetingly, without attempting to verify it. The photographic evidence provided by this testimony unequivocally demonstrates the observation of an artifact. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: photographic artifact (sun).

summary: Short filmed observation of the passage of a bright white object in the night; double clicking sound heard: probable observation of an insect attracted in its trajectory by the light of the flash.
description: On December 3, 2017, at 12:16 AM, while filming outdoors with a smartphone in camera mode, a witness suddenly saw a bright light appear to his right and heard a double click coming from his left. The entire event lasted two seconds. Upon returning home, he discovered that the UFO had been filmed and that the sound was much clearer than he had been able to hear. No other witness statements were collected. Through our analysis (see the investigation report), we were able to demonstrate that the UFO seen and filmed by the witness was merely a small object moving rapidly very close to the lens, probably an insect. This conclusion is based on the following points: - the rapid movement of the UFO, combined with the exposure time of each frame, results in an artificially elongated shape, which is in no way representative of the true shape of this UFO; - At the same time, this movement is probably not parallel to the focal plane of the lens, which results in a decrease in the apparent length of the UFO as it moves; - the automatic use of the flash in nighttime conditions strongly illuminates the UFO, giving it its characteristic white color, and already suggests that it is located close to the lens, the flash range being very limited; - the evidence of two blurs, combined on the longitudinal plane: an anisotropic horizontal movement blur, and an isotropic vertical and horizontal focusing blur. The presence of this latter blur confirms the impression of the previous point, namely that the UFO was very close to the lens, and consequently small in size. The proximity of the lens and therefore of the flash explains why the object, despite its small size, could have appeared as a bright light to the witness's own eyes. The witness heard a noise, which the device recorded and interpreted as a hiss synchronous with the passage of the UFO, and therefore presumably created by the UFO itself. The sound level is comparable to the witness's breathing and could correspond to the hiss of an insect passing by, even if the insect wasn't necessarily large or very close. Explaining the hiss is more difficult for an object other than an insect, as the wind causing the movement would have been recorded. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this as B: probable observation of an insect attracted in its trajectory by the flash.

summary: Nighttime observation behind a windshield of a luminous phenomenon described differently by two witnesses: observation by the driver (T1) of a reflection of the dashboard on a glass element of the car.
description: On November 19, 2017, at 8:35 PM, two people traveling in a car (T1, driver, and T2, front passenger) were intrigued by colored lights seen through the windshield. The witnesses were on departmental road 39, just outside Fouchy (67), heading towards Urbeis (67). The witnesses disagreed on the description of the phenomenon. However, they agreed that it was silent and stationary. They took photographs with their respective smartphones. The two witnesses described the UFO very differently; in particular, T2 described the difference in perception compared to T1 (see investigation notes). Observing the photos provided by the witnesses, it is also noticeable that the UFO seen by passenger T2 is clear, while the one seen by driver T1 is blurry: this suggests the possibility of two separate observations of two UFOs. Two different observation cases are being investigated (see the investigation notes). An examination of the dashboard of the witnesses' car (Dacia Sandero) allows us to identify the origin of the UFO seen by driver T1. By overlaying the witness photos with the dashboard photo, we can see that it is a reflection of the "Media Nav" screen in the windshield, with the presence of a wire or cable in front of it explaining the appearance of two triangles. The red dot is the hazard warning button, and the orange dot is the door lock button. This also explains the silence and immobility of the phenomenon. Consequently, GEIPAN concludes that T1's observation corresponds to a reflection of the dashboard panel on a glass element. GEIPAN classifies case A: reflection. See case [CD39] of FOUCHY (67) towards URBEIS (67) 19.11.2017 T2 to find out what phenomenon was seen by the T2 (passenger) and what classification was given to the case.

summary: Nighttime observation behind a windshield of a luminous phenomenon described differently by two witnesses: observation by the passenger (T2) of an airliner.
description: On November 19, 2017, at 8:35 PM, two people traveling in a car (T1, driver, and T2, front passenger) were intrigued by colored lights seen through the windshield. The witnesses were on departmental road 39, just outside Fouchy (67), heading towards Urbeis (67). The witnesses disagreed on the description of the phenomenon. However, they agreed that it was silent and stationary. They took photographs with their respective smartphones. The two witnesses described the UFO very differently; in particular, T2 described the difference in perception compared to T1 (see the investigation notes). Observing the photos provided by the witnesses, it is also noticeable that the UFO seen by passenger T2 is clear, while the one seen by driver T1 is blurry: this suggests the possibility of two separate observations of two UFOs. Two different sighting cases are under investigation (see the investigation notes). Passenger T2 describes the UAP as four bright points in a cross shape, one of which is flashing in the center. This corresponds well to the sighting of an aircraft, which he compares to a drone equipped with white LEDs at its extremities. Indeed, from a distance and through car windows, it is possible not to distinguish the colors of navigation lights. The photograph clearly shows the twin landing lights of the Boeing 717, which was then on approach to land in Strasbourg. The converging flight path can give the impression of immobility or slight movement. Both testimonies are consistent with their respective observations, and we have photographs (perfectly usable) for both UAPs, as well as an aircraft tracking image for the UAP seen by T2. Consequently, GEIPAN concludes that T2's sighting corresponds to the sighting of a commercial airliner. GEIPAN classifies case A: commercial airliner. See case [CD39] of FOUCHY (67) towards URBEIS (67) 19.11.2017 T1 to find out what phenomenon was seen by T1 (driver) and what classification was given to the case.

summary: Long observation of an ovoid, luminous, opaque and white object at the zenith: movement towards the East: observation of a technological stratospheric balloon.
description: On November 12, 2017, at 5:15 PM (local time), a witness at home observed a very bright, opaque, white, ovoid-shaped object at the zenith. The witness observed the UFO with binoculars in the clear sky: he thought it might be a weather balloon but was surprised because the object was almost motionless. No unusual noise was heard. The witness and the gendarmerie patrol observed this phenomenon until 6:15 PM before it moved eastward. The witness took a photograph (original not sent to GEIPAN). Only one witness statement was recorded. This observation suggested to both the witness and the gendarmes the passage of a weather balloon. This hypothesis was verified with the air transport brigade in Lamentin (972). After consulting the "Flight Radar" website, it was determined that it was a balloon deployed over Puerto Rico that was carried by high-altitude winds toward Martinique. These balloons are part of Project Loon, established to provide internet access to disaster areas and/or hard-to-reach places using high-altitude balloons. Following Hurricane Maria's passage over Puerto Rico in September 2017, the decision was made to deploy a fleet of balloons to allow Puerto Ricans, deprived of cellular service due to destroyed cell towers, to use basic phone functions. GEIPAN classifies this case as A, referring to the observation of a stratospheric balloon originating in Puerto Rico and carried by high-altitude winds towards Martinique.

summary: Long observation of a particular cloud and a beam of light: observation of an atmospheric light column.
description: On the evening of November 9, 2017, around 10:25 PM, a witness from his home noticed a peculiar luminous phenomenon in the night sky. The witness described "a fiery cloud followed by a beam of light." The observation lasted until 11 p.m., the "fiery cloud" gradually dissipating. The witness had time to take photographs. No other witness statements were collected. The witness observed a rare optical phenomenon called a light pillar, also known as a solar pillar or light pillar. This natural phenomenon occurs when sunlight or moonlight is reflected off ice crystals suspended in the atmosphere. It is visible when the sun or moon is near the horizon. It also occurs with artificial lights such as streetlights. In fact, the witness mentioned "the reflection of city lights." However, the light source on the ground must be quite far away, as it is not directly visible. Streetlights produce light sources that can reflect off ice crystals suspended in the air in cold weather (the Carpentras weather station indicated 1.7°C). that day) or in the clouds, and produces luminous columns. In this case, it is the combination of a natural phenomenon (flat ice crystals located lower than usual due to cold weather at altitude) and an artificial one with the presence of strong, point-like light sources on the ground that produces this photometeor. The light sources may have originated from the city of Salon-de-Provence, located to the southwest, like the phenomenon. For more information, see the article Luminous Column. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the observation as an atmospheric luminous column in category A.

summary: Observations of one point then three bright points in the sky and extinction: observation of an airplane in flight.
description: On October 31, 2017, at 6:05 PM, three witnesses in a garden were surprised to see a bright point of light due east. The witnesses then noticed three white points of light that appeared to be at each end of an anthracite-colored object. No sound was heard. The lights went out, and the object disappeared completely. The witnesses observed an aircraft that had been on a flight path heading in their direction for a long time, resulting in an appearance of near-stationary motion in the sky. The aircraft was moving toward them with its headlights on and produced a bright glow as night fell (6:00 PM). This was not a scheduled flight, but an Airbus test flight. The location, altitude, and speed are often unusual for these flights and contributed to the strangeness of the experience for the witnesses. The intermediate altitude (4000 m) and the test context can explain the flight with the headlights on, as these are highly visible from over 100 km away. The attached reconstruction shows the portion of the aircraft's trajectory that was oriented towards the observation point for a considerable time. This portion of the trajectory is over 60 km long, which corresponds to a duration of approximately ten minutes (for an aircraft flying at 200 kt, or 360 km/h). The times and durations are consistent with the witnesses' accounts, taking into account the slight inaccuracy (a few minutes) of both the aircraft's position reports and the witnesses' timings. It has been verified that the direction from which the UFO was observed by the witnesses (around 103° azimuth, determined from the photograph taken by T1, which includes ground references and the Moon) corresponds to the direction from which the aircraft was seen. At the start of the observation, the aircraft was approximately 100 km away, and at the end of the aligned portion, it was about 40 km away. For an aircraft flying at an altitude of approximately 4000 m, this corresponds to a sky height increasing between 2 and 5 arcseconds, which witnesses may have perceived as near-stationary. The photograph of the UFO next to the Moon at the end of the observation shows a configuration consistent with the aircraft's relative positions to the Moon (the Moon was at an altitude of 18 arcseconds when the aircraft was at 5 arcseconds). The decrease in the UFO's intensity was caused by the aircraft beginning to change course and the loss of optimal alignment of its landing lights. The final extinction corresponds to the complete change of course, with the aircraft then being less than 30 km away. Witnesses reported seeing distinct points of light in a triangular pattern at the end of the observation. T1 stated, "The light gradually went out, revealing that it was three lights in a triangle." Witnesses were able to distinguish the aircraft's landing lights (here, an A350/900) since they are spaced approximately 12.5 meters apart for the two on the wings, and the normal eye separation capability is approximately 1/3500 of a radian, or 8.5 meters at 30 km and 6 meters at 20 km (the trajectory data does not allow us to determine precisely what the minimum distance was). In this scenario, the third light in the triangle would then be the one located on the nose landing gear. During a test flight at this low altitude and speed, it is entirely possible that the landing gear was deployed. The triangle formed by the three lights has a height of 14.5 meters and a base of 12.5 meters. When the aircraft is at zero pitch, this triangle is inclined downwards by 18° because the nose light is 4.5 m lower. However, the aircraft is seen from the ground at a height of 5°, so the triangle is seen at a grazing angle of 13° for an aircraft at zero pitch. In this case, the central light has an apparent distance of 7 m from the two lateral lights and can be distinguished. It is, however, difficult to detect a central light lower than the others, and therefore a triangle, especially considering that the aircraft may have a nose-up attitude, which would attenuate or even eliminate the grazing angle of the triangle's visibility from the ground. Another phenomenon can explain the three points of light. They become distinguishable when the initial, single light weakens. This light is then that of the nose lights, which weakens until it disappears due to the aircraft's turn. At its altitude of 4000 m, the aircraft was still directly illuminated by the sun, even though it was two degrees below the local horizon (at 6:05 PM). During the change of course, the vertical tail assembly and the two vertical winglets at the wingtips could have been in a position mirroring the sun, whereas previously the aircraft presented no flat surfaces facing the sun. It is also possible that the roll angle caused by this turn put significant portions of the undersides of both wings and the horizontal tail assembly in a mirrored position. The sun reflection hypothesis better explains the ability to distinguish three points of light due to the large separation (more than 60 m) between them and their triangular shape. This explanation is plausible, but it cannot be proven or disproven. This element of uncertainty is not sufficient to invalidate or even mitigate the airplane explanation, which perfectly matches the geometry and timing of the observed UFO's position. We have three witnesses. Nevertheless, the overall testimony lacks consistency on several points. The questionnaires suggest possible influence between witnesses. There is borrowing of expressions and the use of "we." Above all, despite repeated requests from GEIPAN, the witnesses were unable to provide the source files of the photographs with the attached metadata. It was therefore not possible to use these photos to, in particular, precisely locate or analyze: - the times of capture and observation (a key element for further developing the sun reflection hypothesis), which are subject to certain inconsistencies or differences between witnesses; - the UFO's position in the sky; - the structure (point or not) of the light. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: aircraft sighting.

summary: Low-altitude observation of a bright white point with color flashes and short-distance movements: observation of Sirius.
description: On October 31, 2017, at 12:55 AM, a witness took advantage of the clear skies to look east at the sky and stars (the west being less visible due to the brightness of the moon and the city of Cholet). While scanning the horizon, roughly in the direction of Maulevrier, he spotted a fairly bright white light (east/southeast) with blue and red flashes. Five minutes later, he realized the object had barely moved. He then used the SkyView Free app on his smartphone: the light was not listed. Continuing to observe the light, he noticed it had moved vertically. He also observed that the light sometimes moved in a jerky, rapid straight line over short distances. He tried to take photos and videos with his smartphone, but due to the low light, the point of light was difficult to see (in the photos). Twenty-five minutes later, the point of light was still there, though it had clearly risen from its initial position. The blue and red flashing accompanying the white light continued throughout the observation. The white light was significantly brighter than that of the stars. Only one witness account was collected. A site plan provided by the witness indicated the observation direction at an azimuth close to 120°. A reconstruction of the sky chart using Stellarium showed the presence of Sirius to the East-Southeast at azimuth 120° (altitude 4°) at 0:55 (the time the observation began) and at azimuth 123° (altitude 6°) at 1:10 (the time the photo was taken). The absence of Sirius during sky observation via the app can be explained by poor calibration or a slight discrepancy between the image on the smartphone and the actual sky. A comparison between the witness's photo and the star chart (see the investigation notes) clearly reveals an identical position for the UFO and Sirius relative to other stars. Sirius is the brightest star after Venus (the Shepherd Star) and is never very high in the sky at our latitudes; its color changes are caused by atmospheric turbulence. The "jerky movement over short distances" is a known perceptual phenomenon called autokinetic (l) which occurs when observing a point of light in darkness. The slow, vertical movement observed over 30 minutes is indeed that of Sirius in the sky (caused by the Earth's rotation). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as A: confirmed observation of Sirius.

summary: Observations of the passage of filaments and scintillating discs in the sky; collection and analysis of samples: observation of ballooning spiders.
description: On October 26, 2017, two witnesses on Chambrette beach in the town of Verdon-sur-Mer (33) were intrigued by white filaments falling from the clear sky. One witness picked up a few filaments to examine them. It was then that the two witnesses saw the rapid and silent passage of two shimmering discs moving side by side across the sky. The filaments continued to fall for a few minutes, then everything returned to normal. The witness managed to catch a filament. The witnesses described two simultaneous phenomena: 1. filaments, and 2. discs whose speed, shape, and color did not correspond to any known devices. The hypothesis of spider ballooning fits most of the characteristics described by the witness. Silk threads (also called spider silk) are threads created by spiders to move through the air and on the wind. This method of locomotion is called ballooning. The threads can be rolled into balls, which can give the dual appearance of threads and discs when viewed from the ground. Two arguments might have seemed to contradict this hypothesis: 1. The wind coming from the south or west according to weather records. However, the witness locally describes "a southeast breeze," consistent with the direction of movement and therefore the hypothesis. 2. The distance estimated by T1 and T2 (5000m for T2, 10000m for T1), but we know that estimating the distance of an unknown object is difficult without a reference point. The testimony is consistent, the witnesses credible, with corroborating observations. Following an initial publication in March 2018, the witness entrusted us in mid-September with a sample of a filament recovered during the observation (see section 3 of this investigation report). It was analyzed by a CNES laboratory. This analysis confirms that it is indeed silk fibers mixed with particles, primarily iron oxide (see appendix of the report). This case had previously been classified as B; this new element, which constitutes near-proof of the hypothesis, allows us to classify it as A and republish it: observation of spider ballooning.

summary: Observation of the rapid West-East passage of an opaque white ball without a trace in the sky: lack of information.
description: On October 5, 2017, at 1:30 PM, a witness, lying on the ground during a physical exercise, was surprised by the west-to-east speed of an opaque white ball. The witness noticed no trace left in the sky by the phenomenon. No sound was heard. The observation lasted between 15 and 20 seconds. Only one witness account of this phenomenon has been collected. The witness's observation could correspond to the passage of a bolide (a very bright meteor), although we have not found any formal evidence of this. Daytime bolides are more difficult to see; some can be identified (by cameras or radar) without ever having been witnessed by people. The witness's lying position in a calm environment (breathing exercise) likely facilitated the observation. The described appearance could be accurate, but the indicated duration seems long and would have required further details. The witness did not respond to our request to complete our questionnaire. Therefore, GEIPAN is unable to explore this or any other hypothesis further. GEIPAN classifies this case as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Very short observation of the rapid passage of a colored light across the sky with a downward trajectory: very likely observation of a bolide.
description: On September 10, 2017, between 9:45 p.m. and 10:00 p.m., a witness, who was caring for her child, noticed a bright light flashing by. The object was described as round, on fire, yellow-orange in color, and falling silently. The witness quickly went to the window, but the light had disappeared. Thinking the object might have fallen nearby, the witness searched the following morning, but found nothing. The witness recounted seeing a rather dazzling light for one to two seconds from her window, with the impression that the round shape was on fire. This description joins the numerous testimonies (at least 25) relating the passage of a bolide (entry into the atmosphere of a meteoroid) on September 10 at 19:29 UTC (i.e. 21:29, French local time) visible from Meurthe-et-Moselle to Bouches-du-Rhene, passing through Pyrénées-Orientales, Isere and Switzerland. It also appears that the meteoroid fragmented into multiple pieces at the very end of its luminous trajectory (more details on the website link: REFORME). This fireball was also detected by 14 cameras of the FRIPON network. The time indicated by the witness does not quite correspond to the fireball's passage, but the time given is not very precise since the witness places their observation between 9:45 PM and 10:00 PM, noting that their alarm clock was set to the correct time, but they may not have checked their alarm clock at the exact moment of the observation, which could explain the discrepancy with other fireball sightings. The altitude estimate (4 meters high) was made intuitively. As the phenomenon was very bright, the witness He interpreted it as very close, but without any objective reference point. Fireball phenomena, often perceived as very close by witnesses, actually occur at altitudes of 100 to 50 km, and are therefore visible from the ground over an area of approximately 200 km in diameter. Despite the discrepancy with the time window given by the witness, the appearance and trajectory described leave little doubt as to its correspondence with this fireball, which has been widely observed elsewhere. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": highly probable observation of a fireball.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of an orange triangular object in the night sky: observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On September 10, 2017, at 10:26 PM, a witness on his terrace spotted a low-altitude light moving west. He quickly realized the light was heading in his direction and saw a triangular shape. He rushed home to get binoculars. From his observations with binoculars, the witness described a triangular object, orange in color but with brighter, almost white, extremities. It moved silently along a straight west-east trajectory. The observation lasted about fifteen seconds before the witness lost sight of the object, unable to explain its sudden disappearance (perhaps it was obscured by a cloud). No other eyewitness accounts have been collected. The witness likely observed a Thai lantern. Indeed, all these characteristics: - the orange color, - the eastward direction of movement, consistent with the wind measured at all the weather stations in the area (unfortunately, none have data available within 25 km (here, the Gourdon station at 25 km, taken from Infoclimat), which always has a strong eastward component at that time, - the date, a Sunday evening in summer, conducive to festive events, are all elements in favor of this hypothesis. The witness's objections to this hypothesis hardly stand up to GEIPAN's experience with lantern sightings: - a lantern can be a single device, - the speed can be regular and sustained, depending on the wind at the flight altitude (100 to 300 m), - the flames are not always visible, and even less so directly under the lantern, as they can be hidden by the torchbearer, - the lanterns can have various shapes or cross-sections, particularly in their upper part, including triangular, square, or even heart-shaped (see a commercial website ), - the color of the lantern is not uniform, as the paper can have color variations, especially if the shape is irregular. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the rectilinear and silent movement of a very bright orange luminous ball and disappearance into the clouds: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: While fishing at night on Barcarès beach, a witness observed at 9:13 PM the straight movement of a very bright orange ball of light that quickly disappeared into the clouds. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness obtained two photos from a tourist. The witness most likely observed a Thai lantern. The appearance is consistent with this description in terms of shape, the type of glow (which can be uneven), and also the size (which is never too large; the witness said "fader than the Moon," mistakenly measuring it, as it could not be 3 cm at arm's length). Furthermore, the wind speed measured that evening in Perpignan was perfectly aligned with the trajectory accurately reconstructed by the witness (see Infoclimat). It is early September, in a holiday resort; the location and date are conducive to festive events such as lantern releases. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of about twenty lights in the clear night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On September 2, 2017, at 10:30 PM, a witness observed approximately twenty whitish lights silently passing over Ploemeur and Lorient for one to two minutes. The witness called a neighbor on their mobile phone. The lights were quickly lost from sight as they were hidden by trees in a wood near the witness's home. Only one questionnaire was collected. The witness most likely saw a flight of Thai lanterns; everything in their testimony reflects the multitude of testimonies recorded by GEIPAN for alleged lantern releases, considered confirmed: - the witness said, "They were silent. A light flickered under each device, illuminating it. However, no navigation lights or flashing lights were visible," which is indeed the typical appearance of a lantern; - The entire object was moving in the direction of the wind, which is indeed from SSW to NNE, see measurement taken 4km away (Infoclimat). ; - It was a weekend night, with clear skies, conducive to festive events. The witness refutes this explanation from GEIPAN because: - it's too big: it's common for a witness to misjudge the distance of an unknown object, and therefore misjudge the object's size and speed. It was closer than he thought; - There was no wind: the witness was on his doorstep, which is not an ideal place to assess the wind, and even less so when it comes to wind at 100 or 200 meters altitude (the altitude of the lanterns); - the witness was very impressed and seemed not to believe such a simple explanation. It is common for witnesses to be impressed, see for example this testimony (CHATEAUFORT (78) 10.07.2011). It is also because many people know how to recognize the lanterns that no other witnesses came forward that night. Our witness thinks the opposite and believes that lanterns would have inevitably triggered other sightings. The witness "experienced a unique moment," which is understandable, but it is most likely that lanterns were involved. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Long observations of the evolution of luminous phenomena in the night sky: observations of stars.
description: On August 27, 2017, around 10:30 PM, two witnesses in nature were observing the starry sky. They were intrigued by the jerky movements of luminous phenomena in a restricted area of the sky. Two testimonies were collected. The observation revealed very little strangeness: - when one stares intensely at a star (T1 says "I started looking at a star," T2 says "T1 is fixated on a star"), it is common to have the impression that it is moving; this is the phenomenon of autokinetic fixation. Furthermore, the method of tracking the movement ("I used reference points in the sky, the clouds, or with my finger without moving it") is unreliable, especially in the presence of changing winds and therefore irregular cloud movement (the Angoulême weather station recorded a 90° change between 10 PM and 11 PM (see Infoclimat). - It is not unusual for a star to be accompanied by two other, less bright stars in a triangular formation, provided that the observing conditions are good and allow for the distinction of fainter stars. The autokinetic effect is not necessarily the same for each star, as it can depend on their intensity. - The observation lasted 40 minutes. and the UFO evolves from NW (high elevation) to N0 (elevation 15th below), which corresponds to the movement of stars (and excludes the hypothesis of satellites). The fact that T2 confirms T1's perceptions of the movement does not in any way objectify this movement. Autokinetic motion gives a perception of movement, but its direction and intensity are difficult to quantify and easily influenced by the perception of others. As it stands, to oppose the autokinetic hypothesis, one would need a photo recording, or two independent, precise, and timed observations showing a concordance. And even in this case, the "cloud" origin of these movements would remain the most probable hypothesis given the method of observation used. One might wonder if prior knowledge of a seemingly much stranger testimony in the same location, also concerning a triangle, did not influence T1's perception of strangeness. Finally, the The testimony is of average consistency insofar as what makes it unusual (the jerky movement, the triangular formation) is not very precise in terms of geometry (no drawing or values of movement and angular separations) and sequencing (we only know that it occurs within a 40-minute window). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observation of stars.

summary: Observations of the presence at low altitude of two red and green lights side by side with oscillating movements and a change of trajectory: probable observations of an aircraft.
description: On August 25, 2017, at 2:15 AM (time confirmed by T2), two witnesses observed colored lights (one red and one green) in the night sky, which intrigued them. Initially perceived as stationary, these two lights moved together, changing trajectory, and were quickly obscured by the landscape. No noise was heard. The witnesses most likely observed an aircraft, as the red and green lights were navigation lights. Indeed: - the two lights were always seen side by side or close together, - during the final movement to the right, only the green light remained, as is typical for an aircraft whose right green navigation light is the only one visible when the aircraft is flying transversely at low altitude (as in this case, the aircraft passed and then disappeared behind trees) to the right, the left red light being obscured by the fuselage. The arguments that lead T1 to rule out an aircraft are the absence of noise and flashing lights ("A helicopter or a plane are also ruled out, given the silence and the absence of flashing lights"). However, the perception of noise depends on multiple factors, including distance (witnesses may think the UFO is closer than it is), wind, which can be contrary to the noise (this is the case here with an easterly wind recorded on Météociel), while the witnesses are looking west, and also the strong visual focus generated by the strangeness, which can be at the expense of auditory attention or memorization (numerous examples exist at GEIPAN). Furthermore, the green and red navigation lights were not flashing; the flashing of an aircraft would have come from the white anti-collision lights ("strobes"). While the former are mandatory in all phases of flight, this is not the case for the latter. We can also question the perception of no flashing, at least for part of the observation, because T2 stated, "Then I also saw a green light flashing." The strength of the supporting evidence (green and red navigation lights) and the debatable and inconclusive nature of the opposing evidence (absence of noise and flashing) lead us to favor the aircraft hypothesis. The stationary and oscillating appearance of the UFO suggests a helicopter, which would have presented itself primarily on its left side (red navigation light) before partially pivoting (two red and green lights) and then turning to the right, presenting only its right side (green light). This aircraft does not appear in commercial traffic records, but these records are not entirely reliable, and helicopters are most often non-commercial. It is therefore more likely a private flight, a civil security flight, a medical transport flight, or a military flight. The request for a radar track from air traffic control (CNOA) was made too late, and GEIPAN also knows from experience that low-altitude flights (as in this case) may not produce radar tracks. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B and concludes: highly probable sighting of an aircraft.

summary: Long observation of a fixed luminous phenomenon in the sky: observation of Venus.
description: On August 22, 2017, at 4:30 AM, a witness observed a fixed luminous phenomenon in the eastern sky from the first floor of their home. The witness took photos and videos (tablet and camcorder) during the half-hour observation. Only one witness account was collected. Thanks to a video taken by the witness outside at sunrise showing landscape features, we can deduce that the UFO was located approximately at azimuth 84° at 6:08 AM on August 22, 2017. A comparison with Stellarium at the same time shows the presence of Venus at azimuth 84° with an apparent magnitude of -4. Venus is the third brightest natural object in the sky (after the Sun and the Moon). Enlarging an image of a planet or star is impossible with this type of equipment due to defocusing; that is, focusing on such a distant object is impossible. A point of light filmed with the zoom lens causes optical and electronic artifacts. The observed shape, which varies with movement, is due to the diaphragm. A defect in the diaphragm could be the cause of the shape seen in all zoomed videos (a circle with a downward-pointing point; see investigation details). The colors are chromatic aberrations also related to defocusing. (See case on the website www.geipan.fr, Annemasse (74), April 8, 2012). Furthermore, the witness describes the UFO as a large star "without change" in trajectory and "not much movement." This is a case where the strangeness perceived by the witness stems primarily from what they see through the camera. If he had only seen with his eyes, he might not have given any testimony. GEIPAN classifies this case as A, indicating a confirmed observation of Venus.

summary: Successive observations of the presence and movement of lights in the Parisian sky: observations of airplanes.
description: On August 21st and 22nd, 2017, between 9 PM and 11 PM, a witness on his 8th-floor balcony was intrigued by the stationary presence and movement of lights, which he filmed and photographed. Only one witness statement was collected. This statement was somewhat strange, as it suggested that the individual lights remained stationary for a significant period. In fact, the witness, contacted by telephone, clearly stated that each light, viewed individually, lasted only one or two minutes at most. The same contact revealed the direction of the observation, which was generally southward from the 10th arrondissement of Paris (contradictory information in the questionnaire; the witness indicated the UFO was to the northeast). These two elements naturally lead to the hypothesis of aircraft landing lights from Orly Airport. Indeed, traffic data shows numerous aircraft approaching Orly from the north, with their lights facing Paris. The flight altitude was then between 1000 m and 3000 m, and the distance to Paris was between 20 and 60 km. With a speed of 400 km/h, the aircraft could maintain a near-stationary heading towards Paris (and thus appear almost stationary from Paris's perspective) for 20 km, or 3 minutes. These altitudes correspond to a height in the sky of a few degrees for a witness in Paris with a clear view above the rooftops, a height of the UFO consistent with the photos and videos of the sighting. The aircraft hypothesis is beyond doubt, even more so when the witness specifies over the phone that, for at least one of the lights, this evolution led to the perception and recognition of the green and red lights of an aircraft. One might wonder why the misunderstanding occurred one evening for a witness who had lived in the same apartment for over 10 years. But one might also wonder why the witness didn't mention in their statement the presence of airplane lights associated with one of the UAPs, and why they placed the UAPs to the North-Northeast for an observation from a south-facing balcony. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: airplane.

summary: Observation of the silent north-south movement of a group of about twenty white luminous points: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On August 19, 2017, between 10:00 PM and 10:10 PM, a witness and his wife, on the terrace of their second-floor apartment, observed about twenty white lights moving in formation along a straight trajectory in the clear sky. No noise or trails were noticed during their rapid movement. The observation lasted approximately three to four minutes, with the phenomenon moving south. The witness contacted Avignon airport and the gendarmerie without success. The witness rejected the hypotheses of drone, Thai lanterns, airplane, or space debris. Only one witness account of this phenomenon was collected. The description was consistent with that of a flight of Thai lanterns. The witness's objection to this hypothesis stemmed primarily from the speed, which he estimated to be on the order of that of an airplane. A witness only perceives angular velocity. Here, the movement is from North to South over a 60° vertical arc in 4 minutes. For a Thai lantern flying at a height of 100 m, this equates to a movement of approximately 200 m, or a speed of about 3 km/h. This would be double the value for a lantern flying at an altitude of 200 m, which would seem more likely since the witness sees points of light rather than shapes. However, the wind measured at the nearby station a few kilometers away in Les Cabannes on Infoclimat is precisely oriented from North to South with a speed between 3 and 6 km/h. The station also recorded gusts of 12 km/h, consistent with a hypothesis of flight at a higher altitude (up to 500 m), where the lanterns did indeed resemble stars. To further support this hypothesis, it was summer, a weekend evening, a time conducive to festive events such as lantern releases. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of a cylindrical and vertical object with varied colors in the cloudy sky: observation of an airplane.
description: On August 4, 2017, between 1:55 PM and 2:10 PM, a witness was intrigued by an object at the cruising altitude of airliners. Using binoculars, the witness observed a vertical cylinder fixed in the sky. The upper part (one-third of the cylinder) was reddish-orange, and the lower part (two-thirds of the cylinder) was white, until a large cloud coming from the southwest obscured it. Two aircraft passed almost directly overhead, one coming from the west and heading east, the other from the southeast and heading northwest. Once the cloud dissipated, the observed object was no longer visible. The witness suspected a drone, despite the object's high altitude. No other witness accounts were collected. The strangeness perceived by the witness seemed to lie in the object's stationary appearance, its shape, and its disappearance. The stationary appearance was difficult to assess. The witness reports that the cloud has covered the UFO. The relative change in appearance between the cloud and the aircraft could just as easily be due (at least in part) to the UFO moving towards the cloud. It is typical for an airliner to appear as a wingless cylinder or cigar shape. Sunlight finds fairly continuous reflection on a cylindrical or rounded surface (fuselage, nose of the aircraft), whereas reflections on the wings are certainly much stronger (larger mirrored surface) but extremely fleeting (all or nothing). Judging the verticality of the cylinder is entirely subjective. If the aircraft is moving in the plane containing the witness's line of sight, the fuselage appears vertical. If this plane is transverse to the line of sight, the fuselage appears horizontal. A high-altitude aircraft, without a contrail, can be distinguished for a moment due to the reflection of sunlight on the aircraft, and become invisible a little later due to the evolution of this same reflection. And once it disappears from view, it becomes impossible to reattach binoculars to it. It should be noted that the witness is located in an area with heavy air traffic at all altitudes (at least at this time of day) and that observing this air traffic has already led him to experience strong feelings of strangeness, prompting him to report it to GEIPAN (EMERAINVILLE (77) 05/06/2017). Since it is verified (here through analysis of the aeronautical context) that the observation itself reveals nothing unusual, GEIPAN does not dedicate any further resources to more precisely identifying an aircraft hypothesis (which aircraft exactly) because its probability is so high. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: Aircraft.

summary: Observation of the movement of several very bright and multi-shaped objects flying in the clear sky: observation of Mylar balloons.
description: On July 30, 2017, around 5:30 PM in Le Cannet (06), four people observed, first with the naked eye and then with binoculars, the rapid movement of four very bright points in the clear sky. Numerous photos were taken of these objects, which greatly intrigued the witnesses. The observation lasted approximately 13 minutes before some objects suddenly disappeared or others were lost from sight, hidden by trees. Only one witness statement was recorded. All the objective data collected are consistent with the hypothesis of festive balloons carried by the wind (see the investigation report). The photos help to clarify the chronology of the observation. The factors of strangeness experienced by the witnesses can be explained by: - the brightness of the UFO: due to the Mylar-type surface, which reflects sunlight well; - Sudden disappearance: Due to its surface condition (mirror-like), a decrease in sunlight (clouds passing to the west momentarily obscuring the sun) is enough to make the balloon less bright and indistinguishable, especially considering the strong brightness of the background sky (glare reported by witnesses) behind the balloon; - High apparent speed: The photos taken allow us to estimate the actual speed within the framework of our hypothesis and are within the range of wind gust speeds at that time. T1 considered (but did not see) that UFO 1 had moved over a large distance, but overlooked the possibility that there could have been two different UFOs (these balloons are often launched in groups), as there was no continuous observation. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observation of Mylar balloons.

summary: Observation in the sky of the movement of a bright white point from West to East with a progressive decrease in intensity: observation of the International Space Station (ISS).
description: On Sunday, July 23, 2017, at 11:27 PM, a witness and his partner observed, for less than a minute, the slow movement of a bright white point of light along a west-east trajectory in the clear sky. The intensity of the point decreased as it progressed. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness's observation was extremely precise in terms of date and position in the sky! It corresponds exactly to the passage of the International Space Station (ISS), as recorded on Calsky. The ISS was indeed at its brightest when first spotted by the witness in the southeast at an altitude of approximately 70 arcseconds, before setting towards the east and decreasing in intensity. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observation of the International Space Station (ISS).

summary: Observation of the presence and slow silent movement of colored balls (red and green) in the clear sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On July 13, 2017, at 10:38 PM, a witness in their yard observed a red sphere and three green spheres moving slowly across the clear sky. The witness took photos before the shimmering phenomenon moved away and disappeared. No sound was heard. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness likely saw a group of Thai lanterns of different colors. Indeed, the wind that evening, according to Infoclimat, was blowing southeast in the direction of the observation. This explains the near-stationary appearance of the UFO in azimuth. The slow disappearance may have been due to the gradual extinction of the lanterns. The timing (summer and the eve of a national holiday) is conducive to festive events of this type. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of points of light in the night sky; festive evening of the Tour de France: probable observation of novelty balloons.
description: On July 12, 2017, a witness located in Place Clemenceau in Pau was watching a spectacle during the Tour de France. His attention was drawn to other people looking up at the cloudy sky and pointing in a particular direction. The witness then observed several flat, luminous shapes passing over the roof of the Chamber of Commerce before disappearing from sight. The witness moved to Boulevard des Pyrénées and observed the movements of other luminous points in the sky (straight trajectory and change of direction). No sound was heard. The witness took several photos of the unidentified flying object and also took photos during the day to document his observation. Only one witness account was recorded. An observation in the sky on an evening of spectacle (Tour de France celebration) in the heart of the city could hardly be considered strange without being reported by others, especially since there were other people observing the phenomenon, as the witness indicated. Given the context, it is most likely that the festive and crowded evening resulted in the release of novelty balloons into the sky. GEIPAN will not commit further investigative resources without further reports of unusual activity. GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of novelty balloons.

summary: Observation of the movement of several luminous orange discs in the night sky on the same trajectory: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On July 8, 2017, at approximately 11:45 PM, a witness and his wife were intrigued by the sighting of two orange discs moving along the same trajectory in the clear sky. Several other discs of the same color appeared. All seemed to originate from the east (Gondecourt) and all were heading southwest (Ostricourt). No noise was heard during the observation. The witness took five photos, which were not submitted. Only one witness statement was recorded. The description (colors and shapes) was consistent with a flight of Thai lanterns. At low altitude and vertically, the lanterns can appear as discs. The wind that evening, according to Infoclimat, was from NNE to SSW. It could therefore have caused this trajectory as seen from the ground (described as originating from the North and heading Southwest). It's a weekend, and moreover, it's summer: a time conducive to festive events and the release of Thai lanterns into the night sky. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: Thai lanterns.

summary: Filmed observation of an object leaving orange trails in the sky around 10pm: observation of an airplane.
description: On July 1, 2017, at 10:14 PM, several witnesses observed an object leaving orange trails in the clear sky. The witness filmed the observation. He was then surprised to see other objects leaving orange trails behind them. The trajectories were different. No noise was heard during the observation. The witness suspected space debris entering the atmosphere. Only one witness account was recorded. The video unequivocally shows an aircraft trail. What surprised the witness most was the short, orange trail. It was orange because it was illuminated by the setting sun (which was still shining at the aircraft's altitude). The length and persistence depend on many factors, which could also mean that the trail doesn't exist at all. To a lesser extent, he was surprised by the speed, which was five times faster than that of a commercial airliner. A witness can only speak to angular velocity, and this varies considerably: higher vertically than over the horizon, and higher at low flight altitudes than at high altitudes. The video does not give the impression of exceptional speed. It has been verified that many airliners are flying in that sky at that time. GEIPAN will not conduct any further investigation since the appearance is clearly that of an aircraft. GEIPAN classifies the case as A: aircraft.

summary: Observation during an astrophotography session of a streak then a bright star in space: observation of the passage then the passivation of the last stage of the Falcon 9 launcher.
description: During an astrophotography session at Piton Maïdo on Réunion Island, a witness observed a peculiar luminous phenomenon. The witness described the trail of a shooting star that transformed into a star of intense white light, finally becoming a spherical nebula whose trail took several minutes to fade. The witness sent us their photographs. Only one witness account was collected. The witness observed the passage and subsequent passivation of the final stage of the Falcon 9 launcher, which launched on June 23, 2017 (see the video of this launch here). The launch took place at 7:10 PM UTC in Florida, which is 11:10 PM local time in Réunion. The launcher departs eastward along the equator, and an hour later, at the time of observation in Réunion, it is already at an altitude of 8,000 to 10,000 km, illuminated by the sun and therefore visible from a large area on the ground, particularly in the eastern part of Réunion. The witness's photographic record, reconstructed from the stars in the sky (see the reconstruction map), shows the trajectory oriented due east, linear, and descending towards the horizon, as the launcher will soon pass behind the Earth (as seen from Réunion). The star of light in the photo corresponds to an ejection of passivation gas from the launcher (emptying of the tanks) according to an increasing volume of gas (represented as a star in the photo due to the 40-second exposure time). The disappearance of the launcher's reflection probably comes from its rotation (natural or occurring at the same time as the passivation), changing the sun's mirror effect. The phenomenon is known and has been the subject of several reports, including one from Réunion Island with a similar geometry (it involved an Ariane launch from Kourou: see the case ENTRE-DEUX (974) 21.08.2015 on the GEIPAN website). See also the article in Ciel des Hommes: Luminous halo in the sky of the Indian Ocean on September 29, 2013. The elements and precedents allow us to classify this case as a "Rocket" sighting without needing to commit further GEIPAN investigative resources (in particular for the precise reconstruction of the Falcon 9's position in the sky as seen by the witness). GEIPAN classifies the case as A: rocket.

summary: Observations of flashing and fleeting lights moving across the night sky: probable satellite observation for the first UAP and unusable testimony due to lack of reliable information for the second UAP.
description: On Monday, June 19, 2017, at approximately 10:30-11:00 PM, a witness observed a bright light appearing in the sky below Venus. Its movement and disappearance within a halo intrigued him. After half an hour to 45 minutes, the witness saw the same phenomenon again, almost directly overhead. A photo reconstruction was included with the questionnaire. Only one witness account was collected. This witness provided very precise details to reconstruct the UFO's trajectory. The most precise detail was that it occurred to the right and slightly lower than Venus, in the direction indicated by the photo reconstruction. This reconstruction allowed us to establish that the reference point indicated was not Venus, but Jupiter, which was also very bright that evening. Analysis of the satellites visible this evening (see attached investigation document - reconstruction) allows us to identify one whose final descending trajectory corresponds to that described by the witness in their reconstruction: - it passes to the right of Jupiter (10th to 15th arcseconds to the right). - around 10:50 PM, within the (somewhat imprecise) time window given by the witness (10:30 PM - 11:00 PM). This satellite (USA 234/FIA Radar 2) is visible but at a much lower brightness level than indicated by the witness. However, satellites can produce, in addition to their "normal" brightness, "flares," that is to say, very bright and fleeting moments (lasting from a few seconds to a minute) resulting from a mirror effect between the sun and an observer on the ground. This mirror effect is indeed fleeting because it is conditioned by the orientation of the flattest and most extended part of the satellite. Iridium is a satellite well known for this and whose flares are predictable because the orientation is known. The satellite "in question" here (USA 234/FIA Radar 2, of US military origin and not detailed; see FIA-RADAR) is one whose flares are not very predictable, but fortunately, it has been the subject of observations of very strong magnitude flares (brighter or "Venus-like," as noted by the present witness): - a magnitude -0.5 flare, observed on May 2, 2012, in Ukraine (see the details of USA-234 (FIA RADAR2) bright flare seen). - a magnitude -5 flare (!), observed on April 30, 2012, by the same observer (see the images. - its twin, FIA-Radar 1, flashed at magnitudes -1 and 0 on May 25, 2015 (see the document double flare from FIA-RADAR 1). The witness describes the presence of a gray halo when the UFO disappeared, a halo that is difficult to explain other than by the conjunction of the flare's extinction with the satellite's entry behind a light haze, unnoticeable to the witness as the sky was clear. The correspondence between the UFO's trajectory and that of the flared satellite makes this satellite explanation sufficiently probable to be retained despite this residual strangeness constituted by the halo. The witness describes another Phenomenon: "Half an hour to three-quarters of an hour later, almost directly above me, I saw this curious phenomenon recur, but without the halo." We do indeed have an Iridium flare in this new time slot, but it occurs at an altitude of 34 arcseconds, an altitude that cannot be described as "vertical." We have little information from the witness regarding this second phenomenon. Several satellite objects pass close to the vertical, but more precision is needed regarding this "vertical" position, as well as a direction of movement (which must exist since the witness describes it as the same phenomenon). Perhaps one of these objects is capable of producing fleeting flares. We do not have enough information to investigate this second UAP. It should also be noted that it is common for a witness whose curiosity was piqued after a first UAP to later notice one or more strange occurrences, associating them with the first, which are then identified as unrelated. would not have been noticed without the initial genuine strangeness. Consequently, GEIPAN concludes: - probable satellite observation for the first UAP: B. - unusable testimony due to lack of reliable information for the second UAP: C.

summary: Observation of a fixed, bilobed point of light: observation of Venus.
description: On Wednesday, June 14, 2017, at 5:00 AM, a witness was intrigued by the presence of a very bright, stationary phenomenon in the sky. The witness described a white, bilobed UFO with a red dot in the middle and noted that, apart from the Moon, no stars were shining in the sky. Only one witness account was recorded. What the witness described likely corresponds to the observation of Venus. It is normal that between 5:00 and 6:00 AM in June, Venus is the only star visible in the dark sky. Venus is in the east; the witness mentions southeast, though without conviction, but indicates that the Moon is indeed to the right of Venus and along "a vertical line of 45°," which is consistent with their respective positions. It is also common for Venus to produce a non-point-like (here, the effect of red lobes) and multicolored glow. This results from atmospheric effects (diffracted light rays). It is not possible to definitively confirm this hypothesis. Indeed, the testimony is very vague, given six months after the sighting. The witness did not feel the need to acknowledge the end of the observation (stopped watching after five minutes), nor even to take a photo, which, in addition to the delay in reporting, suggests a rather weak perception of strangeness (during the sighting). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: Venus.

summary: Observations with the naked eye and with instruments of several luminous spheres of varying colors and intensity in the night sky: observations of stars in the constellations of Scorpius and Aquila.
description: On June 10, 2017, starting at 10:30 PM, a couple (T1 and T2) observed two bright, twinkling points in the sky from their terrace. Observation through binoculars revealed a spherical shape and a gyroscopic effect. The two UFOs were also observed through a telescope. The witnesses then observed two other spheres in a different direction, as well as two or three points near the first two. As the situation remained unchanged, the witnesses ceased their observation around 11:15 PM. At 11:30 PM, the witnesses decided to make another observation, but nothing was visible. The observation was repeated the following day at the same time and under the same conditions. On June 12, the witnesses renewed their observation, but again, nothing was observable. Of low strangeness and good consistency (two witnesses), this case turns out to be a case of mistaken identity involving stars in the constellations of Scorpius and Aquila, perfectly visible in a clear sky (see the investigation report). The position of these stars relative to the landscape, as well as their configuration among themselves, corresponds perfectly to that of UFOs. The strangeness for the witnesses stemmed primarily from their abnormally sparkling appearance, with colors (green, red, and white) directed southward. These points seemed fixed but animated. The sparkling effect is perfectly explainable, as these celestial bodies were then close to the horizon. The description of the elements visible through binoculars and a telescope, for its part, perfectly matches that of celestial bodies observed with defocused instruments. The fact that UFOs were seen two nights in a row, at the same time and under the same conditions, is perfectly characteristic of an astronomical misinterpretation. The lack of visibility on the third night can be explained by a change in temperature that greatly reduced atmospheric turbulence and therefore the twinkling. The witnesses did not find this star configuration during their subsequent search with astronomical instruments because they had memorized UFO altitudes in the sky (45 to 50 arcseconds) that were largely overestimated compared to what they themselves had observed near the mountain peaks (10 to 15 arcseconds). The perception of star movement in the sky varies according to the stars' position in the vault; the witnesses most likely compared the east-west movement of the stars that were the source of the UFOs with that of stars much higher in the sky, giving the former an impression of immobility. All the observed anomalies have an explanation. The case is class A, mistaken for stars in the constellations of Scorpius and Aquila.

summary: Observation of 2 lights projected cete to cete followed by a "sort of" cylindrical fuselage progressing eastward horizontally: probable observation of aircraft.
description: On June 5, 2017 (not 2015 as mistakenly indicated by the witness in their free text), between 11:58 AM and 12:03 PM, a witness observed a puzzling phenomenon in the sky. The witness saw, to the Northwest at medium altitude, two lights projected side-by-side, like two beams of headlights. Behind these two lights, they discerned a sort of cylindrical fuselage, the whole thing moving horizontally eastward. This "craft-like object" moved at airplane speed at low altitude, then stopped for the first time, appearing to hover, before climbing to an almost vertical altitude. A commercial airliner at medium altitude approached from the Northeast and seemed to cross the initial trajectory of the "craft." The airplane continued on its course, while the "craft" resumed its horizontal flight on its original heading. Then it seemed to stop a second time, before climbing almost vertically again until it completely disappeared from the witness's sight. The witness believed it was an unidentified aircraft whose trajectory had been disrupted by the medium-haul plane and asked GEIPAN (the French Air Force's intelligence service) to investigate. Only one witness statement was collected. As indicated in the attached air traffic log, the witness was located in an area of high activity (at least at that time) with aircraft at all altitudes, including light aircraft making low-altitude circling flights. Under these conditions, it is unclear what the strangeness of the witness's description might be. A low- or medium-altitude aircraft is distinguishable by its landing lights (which may also be on during the day) and its fuselage. The low-flying aircraft can perform all kinds of maneuvers (for example, training maneuvers), including speed reductions, changes of heading that the witness interprets as significant speed reductions (as soon as the heading changes from "across the line of sight" to "along the line of sight"), as well as abrupt changes in altitude. The aircraft's hovering or vertical climb can hardly be judged from the ground; indeed, the witness uses the words "it seems" or "almost." Under these conditions, the strangest thing about all this is the scenario the witness imagines, suggesting that the low-flying aircraft is an unknown vessel that alters its trajectory to escape the flight path (or the view?) of the commercial airliner. Once it is verified (here, an analysis of the aeronautical context is sufficient) that the observation itself reveals nothing unusual, GEIPAN does not dedicate further resources to exploring or invalidating the scenarios put forward by the witness to interpret or explain a phenomenon that has no basis in reality. It should be noted, if necessary, that the observation was made in broad daylight, in an urbanized area, and therefore a genuine anomaly would hardly have gone unnoticed by the large number of potential witnesses on the ground and... in the air. Finally, it should be noted that the same witness gave a similar testimony two months later (EMERAINVILLE (77) 04/08/2017). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: aircraft.

summary: Long observation of a luminous phenomenon of colours in the night sky: misunderstanding with Capella.
description: On May 25, 2017, at 10:40 PM, a witness on their terrace was intrigued by the presence of a white, yellow, and blue light in the low-altitude sky. No noise or trail was observed. The witness filmed their observation with a camcorder and, upon reviewing the footage, discovered an object with unusual shapes. The witness ended their observation around 1:10 AM, the object still visible in the sky to the north. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. The witness observed the star Capella, which was indeed at the positions indicated in the sky at the beginning of the observation (10:40 PM, 15 arcseconds altitude and azimuth 320° NW), before moving downwards towards the north as described by the witness at the end of the observation (1:00 AM, 4 arcseconds altitude and azimuth 345°, almost north). It is noted that the essence of the strangeness perceived by the witness, and what likely led them to give this testimony, stems from what they saw in the viewfinder or on the camera recording. Clearly, the trajectory and the apparent darkness (the color and blinking effect is typical for a star seen at low elevation through atmospheric turbulence) demonstrate that the object being tracked by the camera is indeed Capella. Furthermore, the witness does not report the presence of a star near the UFO, even though the sky is clear and Capella could only be visible with its location almost identical to that given for the UFO. Under these circumstances, GEIPAN (the French UFO investigation group) is not devoting any additional resources to explaining the strangeness generated by the camera (since it was not seen with the naked eye). Indeed, experience shows that such explanations are always possible, but require efforts that would be unnecessary in this case. It is for this same reason that GEIPAN no longer considers reports focusing solely on strange phenomena perceived through photos or videos without direct eye contact. The present case is intermediate due to the initial (classic) strangeness perceived with the naked eye, which needed to be documented. In particular, the video shows strong lights from streetlights, which can already cause mysterious reflections in the darker areas of the image. It is also known that a strong zoom on a star can lead to all sorts of shapes depending on focusing malfunctions, the geometric and radiometric quality of the device, with a probable accentuation effect when using a video camera (lower quality than a still camera) and when targeting a double star (Capella). Finally, it also happens that the witness zooms in on a light other than the one that initially intrigued them, as framing with a strong zoom is difficult for everyone. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: mistaken identity with Capella.

summary: Observations of the particular movement of a point of light in the sky: observations from the International Space Station (ISS).
description: On May 24, 2017, after an evening spent observing Jupiter with a group of astronomers, two witnesses were intrigued by the unusual SSE-ENE movement of a very bright point in the sky as it moved away and disappeared. The witnesses most likely observed the passage of the International Space Station (ISS). The ISS was located in the directions observed at the beginning (high in the sky, SSE) and at the end of the observation (ENE on the horizon). The time indicated at the end of the observation, 11:45 PM, was 8 minutes off (the ISS pass ended at 11:37 PM), and this discrepancy likely resulted from checking the time later than the end of the observation and/or from the watch being fast. Given the intensity of the ISS in the sky (much brighter than any other star) and its high mobility, it is impossible that witnesses who came to observe a starry, cloudless sky did not see it. The description appears to deviate from a satellite's movement in the sky because it mentions a curved trajectory. However, the description reflects the classic error of a witness: interpreting a change in brightness as a radial approach or departure (i.e., in the direction of the witness) of the UFO. Consequently, the curvature of the trajectory is not seen in the sky (with its rapid changes in azimuth and altitude) but imagined as being in the direction of the witness. The descriptions accurately reflect this phenomenon: - Witness 1: "It was descending towards us while growing larger," "The sphere moved very quickly towards the north/northeast, rising high in the sky until it became the size of a star, then a small, barely discernible bright point, then nothing more." - Witness 2: "A luminous, moving object heading towards us," "A plunging arrival," "It moved straight ahead without descending or ascending before disappearing." The trajectory reconstruction drawing provided by Witness 2 (see questionnaire) shows a UFO coming from the ESE and heading straight towards the witnesses, then turning and heading straight back towards the ENE. A witness cannot detect the radial movement of an unknown object; they can only interpret it, often incorrectly, based on the concurrent changes in its size or brightness. Here, the ISS's brightness increased dramatically towards its maximum position in the East-Southeast and high in the sky, thus creating the "plunging phase of the observation," before decreasing in intensity, probably more slowly than during its increase. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observation of the International Space Station (ISS).

summary: Observation and photography of an orange and curved trail in the sky: probable observation of a kerosene jettisoning from a military aircraft, taking place at high altitude (presumably to limit environmental and population impacts).
description: On May 22, 2017, at approximately 9:45 PM, a witness at his window observed an orange trail in the sky in the direction of Tarbes. He initially thought it was a contrail, but its thickness and especially its curve intrigued him: the witness then suspected a plane in distress. The witness took several photographs and contacted two gendarmerie stations. No other witness statements were collected. Analysis of the photograph and the anomalies noted by the witness (width and duration of the trace's dissipation) leads to the hypothesis of an aircraft jettisoning fuel (see the investigation report). These same analyses allow for the establishment of scenarios regarding the aircraft's position and speed. The hypothesis of a commercial airliner cannot be retained because such an aircraft would have been found on public aircraft tracking websites, and especially because such a fuel jettisoning operation corresponds to a diversion of the aircraft and would have left a trace. On the other hand, given that it was a military aircraft, it is normal that it does not appear in public records, nor in the CNOA radar record, as the latter was made over too short a distance and can no longer be obtained after a two-month period. The CNOA was unable to provide an operational record of the fuel jettisoning; however, the search was conducted too late. (after the necessary investigation time to narrow down the hypothesis) to be able to conduct it across all squadrons in France. Furthermore, such an operation is not necessarily recorded because it is not always a critical operation involving a military aircraft. In this context, the absence of a recording of a military aircraft and a fuel jettisoning operation does not invalidate the hypothesis, which should therefore be retained due to the strong correlation between visual evidence (witness account and photograph) and reconstructions of possible trajectories (photo analysis). The evidence is consistent, with a precise witness account and photographs that could be analyzed. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of a kerosene jettison from a military aircraft, carried out at high altitude (presumably to limit environmental impacts on the population).

summary: Brief observation of a bright flash seemingly coming from a grey oblong shape in the Parisian sky: probable observation of a reflection of the sun on an airplane.
description: On Saturday, May 20, 2017, between 8 and 9 PM, a witness was intrigued by a bright point in the Parisian sky. Seen through binoculars, the bright light appeared to originate from an oblong, silvery-gray shape. The object seemed motionless during the 15 seconds of observation. Only one witness account was recorded. It is likely that the witness saw an aircraft in a fleeting mirror-like reflection of the sun. The witness's first thought was an airplane: "The intensity of the light suggested an aircraft approaching head-on, its headlights pointed in my direction, but the bright point seemed motionless,"... "Motionless, it seemed solid, like a metallic body." The aircraft was seen at an altitude of 20 or 30 degrees, perhaps 20 or 30 kilometers away; the sky was indeed clear. In 15 seconds of observation, its movement was approximately 3 km, which, for a transverse displacement relative to the line of sight, represents an angular change of 6 to 9 degrees (depending on the distance), not easily detectable. The witness recounts the observation through binoculars: "The flash of light came from an oblong, silvery-gray shape. The brightness and color were similar to those of the moon in broad daylight.
