Some areas of the shape were darker than others, notably a small circular section." The sun was present in the west-northwest, on the horizon. Numerous aircraft were flying to the southeast. It is possible that one of them had a heading that positioned its fuselage in exact alignment with the sun, directly towards the witness. The precise geometric condition linking the sun's direction, the witness's position, the aircraft's position, and its heading produces a strong light intensity (only a bright point to the naked eye because the aircraft is far away) and is by nature fleeting: a particular aircraft and a specific brief moment. Viewing through binoculars clarifies the content of the bright point (it is indeed not a star). The oblong shape then visible ("Motionless, it seemed solid, evoking a metallic body") originates from the fuselage, and the darker circular part probably comes from the wing (seen edge-on from the witness's side) and its attachment to the fuselage: the whole constitutes a geometric body distinct from the fuselage, not meeting the reflection conditions, and is superimposed on the oblong shape. This type of misidentification of an aircraft is not unusual. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: aircraft sighting.

summary: Prolonged observation of several fixed lights in the night sky: lack of information.
description: On April 22, 2017, at 11:41 PM, a witness observed three lights in the sky aligned horizontally, with two additional lights appearing vertically a few minutes later, forming a UFO. No movement, displacement, or change in light intensity was noticed during the entire 45-minute observation. The witness photographed the UFO. The witness made a somewhat similar observation on April 18, 2017. They attached two photographs taken during that observation, which may help in understanding the April 22 case. No other witness accounts were collected. The description of the UFO presents characteristics of several prosaic explanatory hypotheses, which can be ruled out based on certain details of the observation (see the investigation report). Unfortunately, it was not possible to verify or clarify certain key points, such as the exact duration of the observation (did it really last 45 minutes, given that we only have photos taken a few seconds apart?), and whether the window was open or closed during the different phases of the observation. Despite several follow-up attempts, the witness did not respond to the questions asked. Furthermore, the second phase of the observation, with the appearance of two additional points of light, is sorely lacking in detail, despite its unusual nature. The case is indeed quite strange. However, the single testimony, and especially the imprecision on key points, coupled with the witness's failure to respond to requests for clarification, give the testimony little substance, insufficient to validate the unusual nature of the observation. The case is classified as Class C; the testimony is unusable due to a lack of data.

summary: Observation of the movement of a bright round shape in the clear sky: probable observation of a Météo-France radiosonde balloon from Brest-Guipavas.
description: On April 12, 2017, at 2:00 PM, a witness was intrigued by the slow movement of a very bright, round shape in the clear sky. He filmed and photographed the phenomenon. Only one witness account was recorded. As the witness suggested, his observation could well correspond to the passage of a radiosonde balloon. Indeed, after checking with the Brest-Guipavas weather center on June 27, 2017, balloon releases take place twice a day at 11:00 UTC and 23:15 UTC. It is quite possible that a radiosonde balloon released in Brest-Guipavas at 11:00 UTC would reach Saint-Brieuc at 1:50 PM local time. Balloons can fly at an altitude of 20 km and are not affected by ground winds. GEIPAN classifies this case B as probably the observation of a Météo-France radiosonde balloon licking from Brest-Guipavas.

summary: Low-altitude observation of a bright point of varying colors that appears to blink: observation of Jupiter.
description: On April 1, 2017, at 10:30 PM, a witness and two other people were intrigued by the presence of a very bright point at a low altitude in the night sky. This point appeared to flash different colors. Only one witness's account was recorded. The observation was consistent with that of a star; in fact, the entire account frequently referred to it as a star ("like a star but..."). What surprised the witness was its larger size and brightness (or "very slightly larger") and especially the change in color. Indeed, that evening, Jupiter was clearly visible in the southeast "above the university hospital building" (as indicated for the UFO). Jupiter was very bright (magnitude -2.45; only Venus was brighter in the sky) and at a low elevation (between 10th and 20th), which allowed for variations in color due to scattering and greater atmospheric turbulence at low elevations. Many GEIPAN reports stem from this misunderstanding; see the GEIPAN website. The mist (seen by the witness) or the clouds present that evening caused the UFO to disappear. It should be noted that the GEIPAN request for testimony made to the two other people accompanying the witness was unsuccessful, which is often the case when the feeling of strangeness is not shared. Consequently, the case is classified as Class A, like the observation of the planet Jupiter.

summary: Multiple observations of different phenomena in the sky over Reunion Island: lack of information.
description: witness reports various sightings of UFOs in the sky, notably one on March 5, 2017, over the sea. On that day, the witness observed a yellow-orange cloud for 30 minutes, within which a black sphere appeared; the entire object changed shape during the observation. Only one witness account was collected. This account is unusable for several reasons: - the information provided is imprecise and refers indiscriminately to different observations; - the photos/videos of the sky supposedly showing UFOs and "invaders" in the sky correspond to the evolution of small, luminous clouds at sunset (yet dark clouds, unlit because they are in the sun's shadow, have similar shapes) or to aircraft (intriguing here because of their black wings and tails...); - the feeling of strangeness experienced by the witness seems to far exceed what the sky actually revealed, and therefore beyond the capabilities of GEIPAN (the French UFO investigation group). For example, the witness insisted on providing us with videos that were rather difficult to understand, but sufficient to understand that it was an exorcism. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Observation in the night sky of the presence of a boomerang-shaped object with flashing white and orange lights: lack of information.
description: In the early hours of March 1, 2017, around 2:00 AM, a witness was intrigued by a peculiar glow in the sky. He described a large, matte black, boomerang-shaped object with white and flashing orange lights. It appeared stationary and silent. Surprised and almost frightened, the witness sat down on the living room sofa. The UFO had disappeared by the time he resumed his observation. Only one witness account was collected. The witness was frightened by what he saw and therefore provided little information. He did not extend his observation in a way that would have allowed him to indicate any possible movement of the UFO and, above all, to describe the end of his observation. The only available information is consistent with the observation of a group of orange and white lanterns, although a weekday night is less conducive to this type of festive event (although a birthday isn't always celebrated on a weekend). The perception of a black shape does not contradict this, as it has been verified that lantern witnesses often believe they see a black shape connecting the lights (a phenomenon of perception). The absence of perceived movement prevents correlation with wind direction and therefore does not support the lantern hypothesis. No civil or military air traffic records explain this observation (but radar does not always detect low-flying objects). GEIPAN does not have enough information to process an observation whose strangeness is otherwise limited, as it remains consistent with a lantern release. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of information.

summary: Observations from a car of an opaque white ball of light moving through a wood and then positioning itself in front of the vehicle; instantaneous disappearance: observations of ball lightning of the "globular lightning" type.
description: On February 24, 2017, at approximately 7:25 PM, a driver and his son, the front passenger, were driving on a small country road surrounded by woods. Suddenly, the driver noticed a whitish ball on his right, moving parallel to their path and in the same direction. This phenomenon then positioned itself in front of the car and seemed to lose intensity. This opaque ball was visible for one minute and thirty seconds before disappearing instantly without leaving a trail. No unusual noise was heard. The description of the observation given by the two witnesses corresponds to a case of ball lightning, specifically globular lightning. This hypothesis is very consistent with the visual appearance, the apparent trajectory, and its altitude. This type of phenomenon occurs during stormy weather, but not necessarily with an active storm at the location. The accounts were submitted to the Lightning Research Laboratory, which unequivocally recognized it as a ball lightning phenomenon. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of ball lightning of the "globular lightning" type.

summary: Long observation from the car and at home of a very bright and static light in the night sky: observation of the planet Venus.
description: On February 6, 2017, around 8:45 PM, a motorist noticed a very bright light in the sky. Upon arriving home, the witness continued to see this light, which remained stationary. She observed it with binoculars. The observation lasted 45 minutes, after which the witness left to visit friends. The following evening, around 7:45 PM, the witness again observed the same phenomenon, located slightly higher in the sky than the first time. Only one witness account was collected. The description of this observation is characteristic of a UFO sighting: - the observation period was long (45 minutes) and the UFO showed little or no movement in the sky; - the UFO appeared two evenings in a row with a sufficiently identical appearance and position for the witness to report it as the same phenomenon: "I noticed the same very bright object in the sky that I observed yesterday." This observation turned out to be a misinterpretation of the planet Venus, which was indeed present, but not in the Northwest as the witness stated, but in the West-Southwest. Analysis of the witness's photograph showing the UFO's position relative to the terrain allows us to refine this position and confirm its correlation with the position of Venus. Furthermore, the witness's indication of the UFO's position the following hour earlier also aligns with the position of Venus (higher and further south). This is reconstructed in the attached document. Venus is brighter than the stars. The colors can be varied and change due to atmospheric effects, as Venus is often near the horizon and therefore seen through a thick atmosphere. This case is Class A: observation of the planet Venus.

summary: Observation of the slow movement of a dark triangle with two white lights: probable sighting of an aircraft.
description: On February 6, 2017, at 7:16 PM, a witness standing in front of his garage observed a dark triangle with two white lights moving slowly above his house. The observation lasted 30 seconds: not long enough for the witness to take a photograph. Only one witness statement was recorded. The witness likely observed a low-flying aircraft. Indeed (see attached reconstruction), the movement of a low-flying aircraft was detected over or in the immediate vicinity of the observation site, both on the virtual radar (Plane Finder) and national radar data. The latter was unfortunately framed near the observation site, but the end of the aircraft's track, heading in the direction of the observation site, can be seen. Both data points show that this aircraft was circling or making back-and-forth movements, which made it possible for the witness to observe it from an eastward heading. GEIPAN did not deem it necessary or justifiable to investigate the identification of this aircraft, which is in any case not unusual as it cooperates with national radar systems. The aircraft's characteristics are therefore unavailable for correlation with the observation, but the observation is consistent with that of an aircraft (in many situations, the green and red navigation lights are not visible from the ground; the white landing lights or ground positioning lights (red) may be predominant). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of an aircraft.

summary: Observation while driving of a row of lights of different colours and some flashing: lack of information.
description: On January 28, 2017, between 5:07 and 5:10 AM, a motorist was intrigued by a luminous phenomenon in the partly cloudy sky. He saw four white lights in a line and two flashing lights of different colors. This observation was made through his windshield. Although driving at 110 km/h, the witness filmed what intrigued him with his cell phone. The testimony initially conveys a feeling of slight strangeness perceived by the witness. It is also (and this may be related) very poorly documented. The video does not show a UFO, but seems to indicate that what intrigued the witness was generally in front of him and therefore in line with his road. The witness also describes the movement of the UFO as being in his direction of travel. The UFO could be Capella, precisely in that direction; the row of lights and the colored scintillation could be caused by the windshield's optics. The witness does not specify the angular width of the row of lights, nor whether the perceived movement of the UFO was due to an angular change or to the idea that its trajectory was parallel to the witness's own (the way a star is perceived to move when it is not recognized as such is that it moves with you!). The description is too imprecise to allow for further investigation: a row of lights seen through a windshield can have various explanations, including the flashing light of a star or an airplane, or the reflection of an object inside the vehicle. Consequently, GEIPAN concludes that the case is classified as C: the observation is not very unusual and, above all, unusable due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation by three witnesses of a fixed greyish object in the sky: observations of airplane contrails.
description: The witness's photograph is characteristic of a horseshoe-shaped contrail. This particular shape is caused by the ejections spreading away from the aircraft's fuselage before merging in its wake. The aircraft's direction of travel away from the witness (rather than moving laterally) allows for a sustained separation of the two contrails. The distinctive feature of the trail in the witness's case stems from the lighting conditions. Very often, these contrails are bright because they are directly illuminated by the sun. Here, the contrail is not directly illuminated by the sun (due to the Earth's shadow), but the background in the witness's field of view consists of a high portion of sky still illuminated by the sun, which allows the contrail to stand out against a brighter background. Moreover, a clear increase in brightness towards the top of the witness's photograph is visible. Flightradar shows several possible aircraft in the direction indicated by the witnesses (southeast of Ancinnes near Aleneon) and at the time indicated (after 6:10 PM local time, 5:10 PM UTC). One runway most likely corresponds to the UAP (Unidentified Aerial Phenomenon) because the aircraft was seen from below, behind the witness, which confirms the upward orientation of the horseshoe-shaped contrail. Furthermore, this runway is indeed in the area no longer illuminated by the sun. The attached "reconstruction" document details these explanations. The witnesses indicate a duration of approximately 10 minutes. This is inconsistent with an aircraft contrail, which moves extensively in the sky over this period. The observation was shorter, and overestimating the duration is a common error. Moreover, the two photos taken by the witnesses, one minute apart, do not show the same contrail. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observation of aircraft contrails.

summary: Multiple nighttime observations of a bright point in the sky with varying colours; the Pan seems to move randomly: observations of stars.
description: witness reported several observations of luminous phenomena of various colors in the night sky during January and February 2017. There was a series of UFO sightings. One UFO was observed by the witness, his partner, and two gendarmes who arrived at the scene. Information gathered during GEIPAN's telephone contact with one of the gendarmes, and subsequently with the main witness, established that there had been a misidentification of Arcturus in the observation made jointly by the witnesses and the gendarmes (0:50 to 1:40 on January 24). The elevation and azimuth readings provided by telephone (witness) did indeed correspond, with Arcturus appearing between 14 and 25 degrees of elevation and between 75 and 85 degrees East. The perceived brightness levels compared to other stars were also accurate. Sources of misinterpretation are quite frequent when this star is observed at low elevation. Atmospheric thickness and turbulence disturb the light rays (scintillation), creating color shifts and the impression of movement. An even stronger impression of movement can also result from an autokinetic phenomenon (see the article the autokinetic effect), particularly when one stares very intently at a point of light. The fact that the witness's other observations also correspond to stars known to create this type of misinterpretation reinforces this explanation. In the evening, around 8 PM, the observed UFO could create the same effect in roughly the same location in the sky, but it was then Procyon. Similarly, the one observed on February 27th at 2:30 AM, and in the opposite direction in azimuth (250° from the other side of the house), could be explained by Sirius (15° elevation). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies all observations as observations of stars (not always the same one).

summary: Observation of two unusual smoke trails in the sky: probable observation of contrails from military aircraft.
description: On January 18, 2017, at approximately 10:10 AM, a witness observed two intermittent trails of gray smoke in the clear sky from their window for 15 seconds. The witness was intrigued by these unusual trails, which did not resemble typical airplane contrails. Only one witness statement was recorded. The observation was not particularly strange. The witness provided no strong evidence to refute their own hypothesis of an airplane (intermittent trails, absence of noise). Intermittent trails are quite characteristic of military aircraft. The absence of noise could be explained in several ways. The aircraft could have been flying at high altitude and without using afterburners (a classic scenario that generates significant noise). Furthermore, any noise from the aircraft could have been masked by ambient noise from the town of Saint-Ambroix. Although the witness stated that there was no external noise during the observation, it is worth noting that the sighting took place in the heart of a town of over 3,000 inhabitants, with a major thoroughfare located near the observation point, namely the D904, a former national highway. Furthermore, the sighting occurred on a weekday, a Wednesday morning. The hypothesis of a misidentification with a fragmented daytime fireball leaving lingering trails is ruled out, since, firstly, the two smoke trails were too far apart, and secondly, the witness observed accelerations. Moreover, this type of astronomical phenomenon is generally seen by numerous witnesses. The accelerations, for their part, are reminiscent of two aircraft maneuvering. Although the UFO has not been formally identified, the description provided by the witness leaves little doubt that it was a case of mistaken identity. The late consultation of military radar data prevented confirmation of this hypothesis. The case is classified as Class B: probable observation of contrails from military aircraft.

summary: Successive observations of intense lights in the sky by a motorist: observations of the sun's reflections on airplanes.
description: On Friday, January 13, 2017, at 5:45 PM, a motorist noticed an intense white light in the clear sky. The glow disappeared for 15 to 20 seconds and then reappeared, brighter than before. The observation was repeated a little further along the route. Only one witness account was collected. It was most likely the reflection of the sun on airplanes. The witness himself suggested this hypothesis but was surprised by the slight movement in the sky, while admitting that it was difficult to assess the movement. He wrote about it, "although they were stationary, well, with the distance... one might not perceive movement well," and it can also be added that the witness was driving. There is indeed a good geometric condition for the sun to reflect off airplanes. Tonight, there is a succession of aircraft flying in the same direction as the witness, heading directly into the sun (approximately 240°). In other words, the aircraft, the sun, and the witness are almost in the same plane, and since the sun is on the horizon, there may be a mirror effect: sun -> aircraft -> witness, created by the underside of the fuselage and even more so by the wings of the aircraft. The phenomenon is sensitive to geometry, the evolution of which with the movement of the aircraft can explain its appearance and disappearance. It is likely that the 20-second interruption corresponded to the end of the phenomenon on one aircraft and its appearance on another, so the cumulative observation over several minutes probably did not exceed one or two minutes of continuous observation on the same aircraft. An aircraft observed initially at an angle of attack of 30° (witness data) descends to an elevation of 20° in one minute and 15° in two minutes. This angular change remains slight and may not have been noticed by the witness. The attached reconstruction shows the final phase of the observation with two aircraft, one located further away and to the south than the other, which corresponds to the witness's perception of a UAP lower and further to the left. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: aircraft sighting.

summary: Multiple observations of the movement of color phenomena during the night: lack of reliable information.
description: witness reported successive sightings on January 6th and 7th, then on February 25th and 26th, 2017: he observed colored phenomena moving in the sky or near the ground. The sightings were lengthy (from 8:30 PM until sunrise). The police officers present found nothing. Only one witness statement was collected (through a questionnaire and telephone calls). The witness described a very strange phenomenon: the sightings occurred almost every night (whether cloudy or not) at ground level (or even on the ground) as well as in the sky, in front of and behind trees. They described mainly lights, but sometimes also something resembling a craft. Noises in the sky and creaking trees were also noted. Photos taken with a computer sometimes appeared to move or reveal the witness's name in the trees. The reported strangeness was so significant that GEIPAN (the French National Group for the Study of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena) wanted to obtain statements from other witnesses present at the scene. However, the witness's wife refused to testify. The witness's friends promised to testify but did not, whether it was the one GEIPAN was able to contact by phone in the presence of the initial witness, or another contacted separately. These two friends described significant elements of strangeness over the phone, which, while similar in nature (lights in the sky and on the ground), only partially overlapped between witnesses. The gendarmes present one evening noticed nothing, but the witness considered the phenomenon to be less intense that evening (but was still present). The refusal of three witnesses to testify significantly weakens the credibility of this testimony. The credibility is too low to validate the strange nature of a single witness's observation. Consequently, the testimony is classified as unusable (C): lack of reliable information. The fact that the gendarmes' observations contradict the main witness's perception only exacerbates the already established lack of credibility.
